To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

new propylamine linked oligopyrrole amides, related to distamycin A and netropsin, linked to a DNA intercalative anthraquinone or heterocyclic system were synthesised, and that some of these compounds show cytotoxic properties against human tumour cells in vitro.
we have developed a new family of combilexines based on a propylamine oligo-pyrrole carboxamide core, linked to a variety of DNA intercalating and DNA groove binding moieties.
we synthesized a series of new potential combilexin-like molecules and that some of them showed cytotoxic activity in cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, DNA binding and biological activity of combilexines as new potential antitumour drugs.
the design, synthesis and biological evaluation of new combilexines with a propylamine oligo-pyrrole carboxamide linked to a heteroaromatic or anthraquinonoid system.
the development of new potential anticancer agents, based on the design of combilexines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these new combilexines are potential antitumour agents.
these compounds have a promising biological activity.
the cytotoxicity and the DNA binding of the synthesised combilexines are not directly correlated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a heterocyclic system is more efficient than an anthraquinone moiety in the DNA intercalation and the cytotoxicity.

the cytotoxicity of the new compounds is not directly linked to their ability to bind DNA, but to a combination of the ability of the compounds to bind to DNA and to inhibit the activity of topoisomerase.
the cytotoxicity of the compounds is related to the inhibition of the DNA topoisomerase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anthraquinone moiety is not an ideal intercalating group, and that the heterocyclic system, especially the pyridinium system, is a better intercalator.
the cytotoxicity of these new combilexines is related to the DNA binding properties and to the topoisomerasel inhibiting activity.
the propylamine oligo-pyrrole carboxamide moiety can be linked to a wide range of intercalators and still retain its biological activity.
